issues.reason: The superlative form is "(Most <scale> X <class>), plus X is a member of the class", while Coordination & plurals states a group is an individual that "never goes in a class slot" and that (GroupOf g sentence) says the members are sentences — so (Most simple sk_group_1 sentence) is ill-typed and asserts the group is the one simplest sentence.

The half that stands is that the second Most repeats the same ill-typed group-in-entity-slot defect; the "no copular atom records the identity" half is the equative-clause coverage gap the reviewer itself files in q2, and symbol reuse is the instruction set's own way of recording sameness.

gaps_confirmed: identity / equative copular clause ("the Xs are the Ys", two definite descriptions equated) — Categorical statements covers only "X is a/an N" and "X is ADJ"
superlative over a plural set ("the simplest sentences") — Most is defined for one entity ranked in a class, with no form for the set of top-ranked members
one-anaphora on a plural ("the most elegant ones") used as a predicate nominal rather than introducing a fresh entity
new_gaps: the mechanical definite-plural determiner rule forces a specific-group reading on a generic aphorism, and there is no way to mark such a group as kind-like, so the empirical-generic confidence dial cannot reach it either
repair_summary: Removed both (Most … sk_group_1 sentence) atoms: a group witness cannot fill the Most entity slot, its mandatory (Member X <class>) companion would be false, and the instruction set offers no set-superlative or equative form to put in their place, so the false content is removed rather than replaced by an invention.
notes: The repair is a net content loss — after removal only the group typing survives and neither the superlatives nor the equation is recorded — which is the honest consequence of the two confirmed gaps.
